preconditions.description: Input integers n and k satisfy 2 ≤ k < n ≤ 1000, where n is the number of nodes and k is the path length threshold.

preconditions.expression: all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.split()) and len(stdin.split()) == 2
preconditions.description: stdin contains exactly two integers n and k, separated by whitespace.

postconditions.description: stdout is a valid text representation of two lines: the first line is an integer c (1 ≤ c ≤ n), and the second line is a space-separated list of integers representing edge colors.
stdout consists of exactly two lines: the first line is c, and the second line is the edge coloring.
The first line of stdout is an integer c, representing the minimum number of colors needed, where 1 ≤ c ≤ n.

postconditions.expression: len(colors) == n * (n - 1) // 2 and all(1 <= color <= c for color in colors)
postconditions.description: The second line of stdout contains exactly n(n-1)/2 integers (colors), each between 1 and c (inclusive), representing the edge coloring in the specified order.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= color <= c for color in colors) and len(set(colors)) == c
postconditions.description: The edge coloring uses exactly c distinct colors, each between 1 and c.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a < b <= n for a, b in edges) and len(edges) == n * (n - 1) // 2
postconditions.description: The edges are ordered lexicographically by start node (a) and then by end node (b), where 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n, and all edges are included exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(not all(color == colors[0] for color in path_colors) for path_colors in paths_of_length_k_or_more)
postconditions.description: For every path of length k or longer in the graph, the set of edge colors along the path contains at least 2 distinct colors (i.e., no monochromatic paths of length ≥ k exist). Here, edges are ordered as (a, b) where a < b, and paths_of_length_k_or_more is the set of all such paths in the graph.
